answer: A sparrow can slip through any open window, so a registry that trusts self-declared names is a fable waiting to be exploited. Require every agent to bond a small stake and pass a non-parallelizable proof-of-work delay before it may transact; the delay is a public signal of real cost, not a claim. An attacker spawning a thousand identities must pay a thousand bonds and a thousand delays, while one honest agent pays once — sybils stop scaling and honesty becomes the cheap option.
